ash: quick heads-up — ran a hybrid quant probe this morning (int4/int8/fp8 mixing) and hit a weird tail-latency regression on sm95 for midseqs (256-1024). p99 jumped ~2.3x on mixed workloads.

mike: ugh. which workload? stable model or a canary?

ash: pickbench sample with llama2-13b, 50% chat & 50% batch gen, prefix cache enabled. baseline (int8) p99 ~58ms, hybrid int4fp8 p99 ~140ms. median roughly the same.

sara: can you paste the perf log? any KV cache miss storms?

ash: logs attached inline: 
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] seq=384 arch=sm95 quant=int4fp8 kernel=hybrid_pick_v2 p50=42ms p95=68ms p99=142ms kv_miss_rate=0.27 batch_size_avg=3.2
[2026-03-17T09:12:15Z] seq=384 arch=sm95 quant=int4fp8 kernel=hybrid_pick_v2 p50=43ms p95=70ms p99=310ms kv_miss_spike=0.84 batches_evicted=2
```

julia: looks like intermittent kv_miss_spike aligns with a fallback to slower kernel path. maybe our hysteresis threshold too aggressive for midseq.

mike: or the kernel selector is oscillating between int4 path and fp8 path on a per-batch basis. that would blow up p99.

ash: exact suspicion. autotune trace shows kernel flips on 38% of requests when seq in 256..512. trace snippet: `flip_count=1230 flips_per_min=17`

sara: what about batch-kick heuristics? avg batch of 3.2 is low; if we delay a sm95int4 kernel until kv warmup it might prefer fp8 and cause eviction churn.

ash: i ran a targeted sweep with `./autotune --arch sm95 --quant int4fp8 --seq-buckets 8 --runs 20 --log=trace.json` and saw latency cliff at bucket 3 (256-384).

mike: can we try increasing hysteresis window temporarily? change `kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms` from 25 -> 80 for sm95 midseq and re-run probe. also try raising `kv_prefetch_threshold` to reduce miss storms.

julia: also suggest a small penalty for switching when `batch_size_avg < 4` and `kv_miss_rate > 0.2`. that will bias towards stable kernel for low-load paths.

ash: running a quick flip: `rdw-autotune apply --arch=sm95 --param kernel_switch_hysteresis_ms=80 --param kv_prefetch_threshold=0.6 --tag temp-hyst` then re-ran pickbench.

runtime-bot: pickbench run completed (1765432188). summary: hybrid int4fp8 p99 reduced to 76ms on same workload, flips_per_min down from 17 -> 2.

sara: nice. can you push config to canary cluster and run 12h stability? also add a metric to track continuous flip_rate and kv_evictions.

ash: will do. starting canary deploy now: `kube rollout restart deploy/rdw-runtime-canary-sm95` — will monitor dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/dashboards/quant-hybrid-sm95

mike: long-term we should update autotune to include a cost for flips in the objective (p99 + alpha * flip_rate). alpha=0.5? open to picks.

julia: agree. open a short RFC/PR for autotune objective change and include cross-arch tests (sm89, sm95, sm99) plus h100.

ash: created ticket RDW-5872 and started a PR draft. attaching the trace artifact and the pickbench command we used.

sara: sweet. one more ask — please run the same canary with a synthetic coldprefix pattern to stress kv-warmup and ensure hysteresis doesn't mask cold-start correctness.

ash: on it. will report back in ~14h. :coffee:
